submission.justification:
Module-D2 at 30% wall coverage achieves the maximum possible light collection of 57.7 PE/MeV, representing a 54% performance improvement over the next-best alternative (Module-D3 at 37.5 PE/MeV). This configuration directly fulfills the primary task goal of "highest possible light collection."

The simulation data demonstrates that light collection scales monotonically with coverage (approximately coverage^0.8), making 30% coverage optimal for any design choice. Among the three candidate modules, D2 consistently outperforms D1 and D3 across all tested coverage levels.

While Module-D2's thin bonded dichroic filter represents a potential failure point in the inaccessible cryogenic environment, several factors support this choice:
(1) D2 has passed cold electronics validation, indicating the bonding has survived cryogenic testing
(2) No bonding failures are documented in project specifications
(3) The substantial 20 PE/MeV advantage over D3 significantly improves physics capabilities for event reconstruction, energy resolution, and low-energy threshold
(4) The task explicitly prioritizes maximum light collection

The 57.7 PE/MeV performance represents the absolute maximum achievable within all project constraints (5-30% coverage, three validated designs) and provides the best foundation for the neutrino experiment's scientific goals.
